page.layout: One page of text, with a running head at the top and the page number at top right. Below the text block: a rule, then the subheading line "Iod. Caph. Lamed." then the verse in one column. No marginal notes. Catchword and signature: none visible; the signature "C 2" is at the foot of the page.

main_text.p:
Vix pellis hæret ossibus ieiuna siccis:
Resecta syluis ligna siccior non sunt:
Cui sanus hostis ense, non truci, pepercit
Illis fuisse quis neget beatiorem,
Quos tardiore languidos fames acerba
Fato peremit: rura quum nullas in urbem
Miserè fruges hostilis obsessa turmis:
Tota nec vllus affuit Syone panis.
main_text.head: Iod. Caph. Lamed.
main_text.p:
AH, etiam in miseros natorum sauiit artus
Furente mater dextera.

Humanosque omnes affectus pectore pellens,
Et caritatis immemor
Materna, immiti corpuscula dente vorauit
Infantium tenellula:

Quum male suada fames totam grassata per urbe
Cines Syonis abstulit.

Nam Rex Cœlitum iustas accensus adiras,
Seuerus ille criminum
Vindex, in Solymam cœli de sede furores
Effudit omnes ardua.

Protinus & flammis celsas crepitantibus arces,
Et cuncta tecta perdidit.

Atque alto feruens à culmine funditus urbem
Syonis omnem subruit.
Qui reges toto dominantur in orbe, feraces

page.notes: The first block of verse is in italic type and was transcribed as such in print; the initial "A" is a large woodcut-style initial joined to "H," as "AH,". The line "Miserè fruges" and similar lines are read from a small, slightly blurred scan; "obsessa" and "turmis" are uncertain, so they should be checked against the original. Line 1 of the first block ("siccis:") and "Resecta" should be checked, as the scan is faint at the left edge. The Hebrew-style acrostic headings "Iod. Caph. Lamed." are small capitals in the printed page and are given level 2. The word "Syone" is printed as such. The page number "35" is printed at top right; the signature "C 2" is printed at bottom right of the text block. The printed lines of the first verse block are italic, and the words "Quos", "Humanosque" and "Atque" begin with a capital in the printed form.
